newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Jan 21.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Jan 21.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Investment bank Macquarie Bank Ltd said on Monday afternoon that one of its executives, Simon Hannes, had been charged under the Financial Transaction Reports Act in connection with an investigation into option trading in TNT Ltd. Macquarie said it believed Hannes intended to plead not guilty.
* Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$18.60 (-0.10)

The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) said late on Monday its steel division had advised Port Kembla steelworks would lose about 100,000 toness of iron production after a breakout of molten iron at No. 5 Blast Furnace last Friday. It also reported on Monday higher copper, steel and petroleum products output for December but lower coal production.

Westpac Banking Corp said on Monday trading in the three months ended December 31 was "reasonably on track". "We are reasonably on target for what we have been expecting in the first quarter," Westpac managing director Bob Joss told reporters after the bank's annual meeting. Earlier Westpac's Chairman John Uhrig said that intense competition may put further pressure on lending margins. It also said that full franking of dividends would be maintained in the foreseeable future.

Intellect Holdings Ltd said it will make a takeover offer for Techway Ltd in a counter-bid to a previous offer by Nova Pacific Capital Ltd. Intellect said it will offer one of its shares for every 2-1/2 Techway shares. Based on Monday's closing price of 98 cents for Intellect, the offer values each Techway share at 39.2 cents and Techway's 12.6 million issued shares at A$4.9 million.

British geoscience service company Scott Pickford Plc said on Monday it was still in discussions with two interested takeover suitors -- Core Laboratories of the U.S. and Australia's Aerodata Holdings Limited -- to establish a price at which a deal could be done.
St Barbara announced late on Friday its net profit for the first half of the year fell to A$3.07 million from A$8.73 million in the previous corresponding half year.
